export const meta = {
  name: 'prover-in-the-toolkit-oracle-continuation',
  description: 'Relaunch the 16 oracle-research cells as continuation sessions in their existing sandboxes',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Oracle research (continuation)', detail: '2 tasks x 2 arms x 4 replicates, same sandboxes' },
  ],
}

const ROOT = '<scratchpad>/runs'

const ORACLE_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    sandbox: { type: 'string' },
    task: { type: 'string' },
    arm: { type: 'string' },
    claims_complete: { type: 'boolean', description: 'whether RESULT.md claims the completed bundle characterizes the reference' },
    claim_grounds: { type: 'string' },
    admitted_families: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { name: { type: 'string' }, description: { type: 'string' }, file: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['name', 'description'] } },
    added_laws: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { name: { type: 'string' }, statement: { type: 'string' }, tolerance: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['name', 'statement'] } },
    correct_variants_checked: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    lean_file: { type: 'string', description: 'path of the Lean file, or empty if none' },
    lean_main_theorem: { type: 'string' },
    lean_compiled: { type: 'boolean' },
    primitive_assumptions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'every assumption made about exp/sqrt/log etc., one statement each' },
    statement_vs_laws: { type: 'string', description: 'how the Lean statement differs from what laws.py checks' },
    remarks_on_formal_ambiguity: { type: 'string' },
    elapsed_seconds: { type: 'number' },
    outside_paths_read: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    inherited_files_used: { type: 'string', description: 'what the interrupted previous session had left, and what you kept, verified or discarded' },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['sandbox', 'task', 'arm', 'claims_complete', 'claim_grounds', 'admitted_families', 'added_laws', 'elapsed_seconds', 'outside_paths_read', 'inherited_files_used'],
}

const prompt = (dir, task, arm) => `You are a research agent. Your working directory, and the ONLY directory you may read, write or search in, is:

${dir}

A previous session started this task in this same directory and was cut off by an external limit before it could write RESULT.md or report. You have no memory of it. Its files are present (admitted kernels, draft laws, draft proofs, scratch). They are yours: inventory them first (\`ls -R\`), re-run \`venv/bin/python gate.py\` on anything they claim, and keep, repair or discard them on their merits — you are accountable for everything that ends up in the directory.

Start by running \`date +%s\` and then reading ${dir}/README.md; it is the complete task statement and it is authoritative. Follow it to the letter. Use ${dir}/venv/bin/python for all Python. Do not read, search or open anything outside that directory; do not use the network. Work until you have a result you can defend, with every claim demonstrated by a file in the directory. Write RESULT.md as the README asks (say in it what you inherited and what you did with it), run \`date +%s\` again, and then return the structured report (task "${task}", arm "${arm}", sandbox "${dir}"). The structured report is the return value; RESULT.md is the human record. Both must agree.`

const cells = []
for (const task of ['softmax', 'layernorm'])
  for (const arm of ['T', 'F'])
    for (const r of [1, 2, 3, 4])
      cells.push({ task, arm, r, dir: `${ROOT}/oracle/${task}-${arm}-r${r}` })

log(`relaunching ${cells.length} oracle-research continuation sessions`)
const results = await parallel(cells.map(c => () =>
  agent(prompt(c.dir, c.task, c.arm), { label: `oracle:${c.task}-${c.arm}-r${c.r}`, phase: 'Oracle research (continuation)', schema: ORACLE_SCHEMA })
    .then(x => ({ cell: c, report: x }))))
const done = results.filter(Boolean)
log(`${done.filter(x => x.report).length}/${cells.length} sessions returned a report`)
return { oracle: done, missing: cells.length - done.length }

report.claim_grounds: Over the reals, in exact arithmetic, the completed bundle {FINITE_OUTPUT, UNIT_INTERVAL, ROW_SUMS, SHIFT_INVARIANCE, LOG_ODDS} is satisfied by reference.py's function and by no other kernel R^{m x n} -> R^{m x n}, for every shape. Proof (RESULT.md Proposition 4): LOG_ODDS says y_rj = e^{k_r} e^{x_rj} with y > 0; ROW_SUMS gives e^{k_r} = 1/sum_j e^{x_rj}; so y = softmax(x). Conversely softmax satisfies both. Already {ROW_SUMS, LOG_ODDS} suffices, and one added law is the smallest completion because the frozen bundle alone admits exactly Phi o C (C = row centering, Phi ANY map into the simplex; Proposition 1), a set as large as the set of all functions. Demonstrated: 17 admitted kernels in admitted/ plus 44 random Phi (analysis/random_phi_sweep.py) pass gate.py --no-laws (0/9) and are rejected by the reference arm and by the completed bundle (6-7/9, identical group counts); reference plus 8 correct rewrites pass every arm with log-odds ratio <= 0.56 on the gate and <= 0.85 over 1440 random inputs each (analysis/results.md, analysis/out/false_positive_sweep.txt). Proposition 3 explains why no weaker law could do it: the temperature family softmax(beta x) lies in the admitted set and is exactly the set of kernels definable with an abstract exponential satisfying E(a+b)=E(a)E(b), so the completing law must carry exp's normalization (here via log). Not claimed: floating-point equivalence beyond the stated tolerance; inputs the gate never generates; a tolerance-free completion (conjectured impossible, not proven); a machine-checked proof.

admitted_families.name: Phi o C (the whole admitted set)
admitted_families.description: Proposition 1: a kernel satisfies the frozen bundle over the reals iff K = Phi o C with C(x) = x - rowmean(x) 1^T and Phi any function from centered matrices into the product of simplices. Constructor admitted(phi); 44 random instances (30 tanh nets, 10 linear maps, |c|, sin 3c, c^2-c, renormalized 1/(1+c^2)) in analysis/random_phi_sweep.py: frozen bundle admits 41/44 (3 fail SHIFT_INVARIANCE only through float32 partner quantization, ratio 0 with an exact partner), completed bundle and reference arm reject 44/44.

admitted_families.name: temperature_2
admitted_families.description: softmax(x/2): temperature error (a forgotten or doubled 1/sqrt(d) scale). Frozen 0/9, completed 7/9, reference 7/9. Fitted log-linear slope 0.5.

admitted_families.name: base2_missing_log2e
admitted_families.description: exp2(x - m) without the log2(e) factor = softmax at temperature 1/ln 2; the realistic base-2 optimizer's bug. Fitted slope 0.6931. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: squared_normalized
admitted_families.description: softmax(x)^2 renormalized = softmax(2x): a post-processing bug that is a temperature error in disguise. Fitted slope 2. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: reversed_sign
admitted_families.description: softmax(-x): temperature -1, favours the smallest logit. Fitted slope -1. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: uniform
admitted_families.description: 1/n everywhere, ignores the input (temperature 0 / E = 1). 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: hardmax
admitted_families.description: one-hot at the row argmax (temperature -> 0 limit); produces exact zeros. 0/9 -> 7/9 (caught by the zero-where-normal FAIL of LOG_ODDS).

admitted_families.name: sparsemax
admitted_families.description: Euclidean projection of each row onto the simplex (Martins & Astudillo 2016), a genuine literature alternative; shift-invariant, exact zeros. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: first_column_onehot
admitted_families.description: one-hot at column 0 regardless of input (uninitialized-buffer style). 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: label_smoothing
admitted_families.description: 0.9 softmax(x) + 0.1/n: a fused smoothed softmax that was meant to be plain. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: prior_weighted
admitted_families.description: softmax(x + log w) for a fixed non-uniform column prior w: the family even full tilt equivariance admits (Proposition 6); only the base point K(0) = uniform separates it. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: fast_exp_squaring
admitted_families.description: exp approximated by (1 + t/256)^256: up to 7% relative error at t = -6, yet positive, renormalized and a function of x - rowmax. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: rational_phi
admitted_families.description: phi(t) = 1/(1 - t) in place of exp(t), t = x - rowmax: any positive phi renormalized is admitted. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: cubic_centered
admitted_families.description: softmax of the cube of the centered input: non-monotone, not a temperature. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: random_phi
admitted_families.description: a fixed random two-layer tanh map of the centered input pushed into the simplex: an arbitrary function. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: rank_based
admitted_families.description: output proportional to the within-row rank of each entry. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: columns_reversed
admitted_families.description: correct softmax values stored in reversed column order (reversed store index in a tiled kernel): multiset per row is right. 0/9 -> 7/9.

admitted_families.name: row_rotated
admitted_families.description: output row i is softmax of input row i+1 (off-by-one row index): each row is a softmax of some row, and every row was shifted by a constant. 0/9 -> 6/9 (identity on the three single-row groups).

added_laws.name: LOG_ODDS (log_odds_match_input_differences, laws.py)
added_laws.statement: For every input and every row r there is a constant k_r such that y_rj > 0 and log y_rj - x_rj = k_r for all j; equivalently log(y_ri / y_rj) = x_ri - x_rj for every pair (the output's log-odds equal the input's differences). Case property, tier portable, not tolerance-free, defers non-finite output to outputs_are_finite and negative output to values_in_unit_interval; FAILs on an output shape different from the input's and on a zero output where the exact softmax value is a normal number of y's dtype.
added_laws.tolerance: Residual r_rj = (log y_rj - x_rj) - (log y_r* - x_r*) anchored at the row argmax r* (t = 0 there), in float64. Per-entry budget eps(y.dtype) * (L + |t_rj|), L = max(log2 n, 1), t_rj = x_rj - max_r x: the L term is the harness's usual O(log2 n) eps arithmetic-rounding budget (exp ulps + pairwise sum + division, doubled for the difference of two relative errors), the |t| term is the half-ulp argument rounding of x - max (and of a base-2 rescaling) in the kernel's working precision, which is absolute in the exponent hence relative in y. Computed through the harness's own residual_ratio on r / (1 + |t|/L) against a zero reference (documented unit-scale fallback = absolute deviation in units of eps log2 n), judged with within_threshold at the LAPACK constant 30. Entries with t < log(tiny) + log(n) (exact value cannot be a normal float) are not judged; none occur in the gate's domain. Measured ratio: reference 0.20, correct variants 0.31-0.551 on the gate; zero failures and max 0.85 over 9 correct kernels x 1440 random inputs at scales sigma = 0.3..10 (analysis/out/false_positive_sweep.txt). Temperature error detected from delta ~ 7.5e-6..1e-5 (reference arm: 1.8e-5), matching the prediction 30 eps (L + ptp)/ptp within one grid step.

report.inherited_files_used: The interrupted session left: 17 admitted kernels plus the Phi o C constructor (admitted/), 7 correct variants, the complete LOG_ODDS law in laws.py, 7 analysis scripts with saved outputs and a master table (analysis/), and no RESULT.md although laws.py, _family.py and the analysis scripts cited "Proposition N (RESULT.md)" by number. I inventoried everything and re-ran every claim. KEPT after verification: all 17 admitted kernels (each re-verified frozen 0/9, completed 6-7/9, reference 6-7/9), all 7 correct variants (0/9 on every arm), laws.py (reviewed line by line; logic sound), all analysis scripts (hierarchy, tilt_equivariance, random_phi_sweep reproduced their saved outputs byte for byte). REPAIRED: laws.py's docstring cited measured ratios from an older version of the law (<= 1.4; sweep 'flat') -> corrected to current measurements (<= 0.56; <= 0.85); analysis/sensitivity.py's predicted threshold ignored the |t| rescaling (predicted 2.3e-6 vs measured 7.5e-6) -> corrected to 30 eps (L+ptp)/ptp, now within one grid step of every measurement. REGENERATED (stale): analysis/out/dead_ends.txt, sensitivity.txt, false_positive_sweep.txt and results.md/json carried pre-rescaling numbers (worst gate ratio 1.37 vs 0.551 now; sweep at sigma=10 read 12.7 vs 0.85 now); run_all.txt showed a garbled first-law column '8)' that the current code does not produce (stale output, not a live bug); shift_law_margin.txt was missing and was created. ADDED: correct_variants/polynomial_exp.py (hand-rolled range-reduced degree-7 polynomial exp in float32; passes every arm, ratio 0.334), analysis/kernels/small_entry_perturbed.py (probe showing the per-entry relative law catches a 1e-4 tail error on 6/9 groups where the reference arm catches 1/9), RESULT.md with Propositions 1-7 written out and proved. DISCARDED: nothing; everything inherited stood on its merits after re-verification. reference.py, bundle.yaml, gate.py and autokernel_pbt/ were read only.
primitive_assumptions: exp : R -> (0, inf) is strictly positive on all of R (used for y > 0 in Proposition 4 and for the zero-where-normal FAIL)
exp(a + b) = exp(a) exp(b), hence exp(0) = 1 (used in Propositions 3, 4, 5, 6: factoring e^{k_r} e^{x_rj}, and tilt_v o tilt_x = tilt_{x+v})

log is the inverse of exp on (0, inf): log(exp(a)) = a and exp(log(p)) = p for p > 0 (used to pass between LOG_ODDS and y_rj = e^{k_r} e^{x_rj}; this is the property that pins the base of the exponential and that the abstract-exponential axioms lack)
the continuous solutions of E(a + b) = E(a)E(b) with E > 0 are exactly E(a) = exp(beta a), beta in R (Cauchy's exponential equation; used only in Proposition 3)
a row sum equal to one determines the positive normalizing constant uniquely (division in an ordered field)
max and argmax of a finite real row exist and x_rj - max_r x <= 0 with equality at the argmax (used for the anchor and for the non-judged region)

floating point only (tolerance argument, not the characterization): np.exp / np.exp2 / np.log are accurate to a few ulps; IEEE binary32 has eps = 2^-23 and tiny = 2^-126; x - max is computed with at most half an ulp of error; pairwise summation of n terms accrues O(log2 n) ulps and sequential at most n - 1; np.log in float64 on float32 data has relative error ~2^-53
np.sqrt and rsqrt-style reciprocals are correctly rounded or within a few ulps (used only to argue the rsqrt_squared variant is correct; it was also checked empirically)
report.remarks_on_formal_ambiguity: (1) 'Characterize on every input in the gate's domain': the gate's domain is float32 N(0,1) matrices of nine fixed shapes plus one shifted partner each; I read the question as being over all real matrices of each shape (the propositions hold for every m, n >= 1) and treated the gate's 18 cases as the demonstration, not the quantifier. (2) 'Kernel' is taken as any map R^{m x n} -> R^{m x n}; an output of a different shape is treated as breaking the signature (LOG_ODDS FAILs it; ROW_SUMS and the reference arm also react). (3) For n = 1 the admitted set is already {softmax} (Delta_1 = {1}), so the two single-column rungs are blind for every arm and every kernel's 7/9 is 7 of the 7 groups with n >= 2; this is a property of the task, not a gap. (4) FINITE_OUTPUT is vacuous over the reals and UNIT_INTERVAL's upper bound follows from the lower bound plus ROW_SUMS, so the frozen bundle's real content is {rows in the simplex, invariance under per-row translation}. (5) LOG_ODDS is stated existentially (there exists k_r per row); the implementation realizes the existential by anchoring at the row argmax, which is equivalent in exact arithmetic. (6) SHIFT_INVARIANCE is kept in the completed bundle although it is redundant over the reals, because its floating-point job (the overflowing no-max-subtraction kernel, which over the reals IS softmax) is real; the characterization question and the floating-point detection question are different questions and RESULT.md keeps them apart. (7) 'Smallest set of additional laws' is read as cardinality: one law, since zero cannot suffice; {ROW_SUMS, LOG_ODDS} is also a minimal characterizing subset of the completed bundle.
report.statement_vs_laws: The exact statement is: for all x, for all r, there is k_r with y_rj > 0 and log y_rj - x_rj = k_r for all j. laws.py checks a tolerant, partially abstaining version: (a) equality is replaced by max_rj |r_rj| / (eps (L + |t_rj|)) < 30 with r anchored at the row argmax, so any kernel whose log-odds residual is within that budget passes (temperature errors below ~7e-6, exp approximations with relative error below ~3e-5 per entry) — the same kind of slack the reference arm has at 30 eps log2(n) max|y|, measured per entry relatively rather than in max-norm absolutely (which is why the probe small_entry_perturbed is caught 6/9 by the law and 1/9 by the reference arm); (b) entries whose exact value cannot be a normal float (t < log(tiny) + log n) are not judged at all, whereas the real statement constrains them; none occur in the gate's domain; (c) non-finite or negative outputs are INCONCLUSIVE for this law (deferred to outputs_are_finite / values_in_unit_interval) rather than violations, so the completed bundle as a whole, not this law alone, is what rejects them; (d) an exact dtype is INCONCLUSIVE; (e) the law is evaluated on the gate's 18 fixed cases, not on all inputs. The characterization claim is about the real functions the laws define (Proposition 4); the gate results are the demonstration that the implemented laws agree with those definitions on every kernel in the directory.

correct_variants/exp2_log2e.py — base-2 exponentiation with a log2(e) factor, float32 (ratio 0.551)
correct_variants/reciprocal_multiply.py — one reciprocal per row, multiply instead of divide (0.310)
correct_variants/float32_sequential.py — all float32 with a sequential (cumsum) row sum, the worst case for the log2 n budget (0.334)

correct_variants/log_domain.py — via log-softmax, exp((x - m) - log sum exp) (0.527)

all nine correct kernels also pass the false-positive sweep (12 shapes up to (2, 4096) x 30 seeds x sigma in {0.3, 1, 3, 10}: zero failures, max ratio 0.85) and the out-of-harness tilt-equivariance test (ratio <= 0.66)
report.notes: Key files: laws.py (the completion), RESULT.md (Propositions 1-7 with proofs, inherited-files account, claim and non-claims), analysis/results.md (master table: 29 kernels x {frozen, completed, reduced, reference}), analysis/out/*.txt (one per analysis). Additional findings recorded in RESULT.md section 5: the frozen bundle's only real detection (naive float32 overflow) is a floating-point fact with no counterpart over the reals; SHIFT_INVARIANCE in float32 is a Lipschitz test on the partner's quantization (|fl32(x+c) - c - x| up to 4.5e-4) with a 2.5-6x margin for the reference itself (gate ratios up to 4.1, max 11.7 over 400 random groups) and it rejects 3 of 44 exactly invariant random Phi; dead ends: a ptp-scaled log-odds formulation false-positives on near-constant rows (ratio 350 at spread 1e-4), a tolerance-free tie law is not backend-safe (lane_split_exp violates it on 16/64 tied rows), and no group law on the shift_rows partner can complete the bundle since the partner's output equals the base's on the whole admitted set (Proposition 7); the metamorphic completion the harness cannot express (tilt equivariance + base point, Proposition 6) is demonstrated outside gate.py and admits exactly the prior-weighted softmaxes without the base point. Hygiene note: two oversized cat outputs were auto-persisted by the tool harness to its own tool-results folder outside the sandbox; I did not open those files and re-read the same content from inside the sandbox in smaller pieces, so no outside path was read. No Lean or other proof assistant exists inside the sandbox, so the proofs are paper proofs; lean fields are empty accordingly.

report.claim_grounds: In exact arithmetic over the reals, for kernels R^{m x n} -> R^{m x n}: bundle.yaml plus the one law log_ratio_to_input (y > 0 and x_j - log y_j constant within every row) admits the reference and nothing else, on the gate's domain and every domain. Proof: y_j = exp(x_j - c) and rows summing to one force exp(-c) = 1/sum exp(x_k); mechanized as SoftmaxBundle.completion_characterizes (=>) and softmax_satisfies (<=) in proofs/SoftmaxBundle.lean, compiled with Lean 4.34.1 core (proofs/lean_build.log, exit 0). Theorem 1 (admitted set of the original bundle = {F o q}, F arbitrary into the simplices) mechanized as admitted_iff_factor; Theorem 3 (every completion needs a non-scale-invariant law) in proofs/ScaleBlindness.lean. Empirically: 14 admitted kernels and 50 random draws from the admitted set are rejected by the completed bundle on exactly the groups the reference arm rejects (gate_results.txt, lattice_table.txt, random_admitted.txt); reference and six correct float32 rewrites pass with max test ratio 1.24 vs threshold 30 (tolerance_margins.txt), 0 false alarms over 20 extra seeds x 9 groups x 7 kernels (seed_sweep.txt). Not claimed: anything about floating point beyond what was measured, tightness of the threshold, closure of the abstention gap for kernels that raise, float16.

admitted_families.name: scaling orbit softmax(beta*x)
admitted_families.description: every law of the bundle is invariant under x -> beta*x (Theorem 3); members: temperature_half (beta=1/2), softmin (-1), base2_missing_log2e (ln 2, the exp2-without-log2e slip), uniform (0), argmax_onehot (limit 0+). Reference arm rejects 7/9 groups; bundle 0/9.

admitted_families.name: non-Gibbs normalized f(x - max)
admitted_families.description: y = f(z)/sum f(z) for an arbitrary positive f; Taylor softmax f = 1 + z + z^2/2.

admitted_families.name: Gibbs of a curved exponent
admitted_families.description: softmax of a quadratic in z agreeing with x at the row's extremes; passes unit_temperature, fails gibbs_log_linear (independence witness for the factoring).

admitted_families.name: vertex-valued / sparse simplex maps
admitted_families.description: hard argmax one-hot; sparsemax (Euclidean projection onto the simplex, exact zeros).

admitted_families.name: output permutations
admitted_families.description: softmax with columns written back in reverse order (indexing bug).

admitted_families.name: row mixing (F not row-separable)
admitted_families.description: output row i is softmax of input row i+1 mod m; still shift-invariant because the shift law adds a constant to every row. Reference arm rejects 6/9.

admitted_families.name: shape-dependent patchwork
admitted_families.description: the admitted set is a product over shapes: correct on full 8-wide tiles, temperature 1/2 on ragged tail columns; rejected on 3/9 groups only.

admitted_families.name: convex mixtures (the admitted set is convex)
admitted_families.description: (softmax + 1/n)/2 and (1-eps) softmax + eps/n with eps = 1e-3; admitted for every eps in (0,1], so the bundle's resolution is the diameter of the simplex (resolution_sweep.txt).

admitted_families.name: wrong output type (harness blind spot)
admitted_families.description: returns [[1.0]] for every input; all four bundle laws read y alone so it is admitted on every shape; reference arm FAILs the shape mismatch 8/9. Closed by output_type_matches_input.

admitted_families.name: random F on the shift quotient
admitted_families.description: random tanh network, piecewise-constant per-row temperature switch, argmax mixture, column permutation: 40/40 admitted by the bundle, 40/40 rejected by reference arm and completed bundle; the smooth per-row temperature field (10 draws) is admitted in exact arithmetic but rejected by the float32 shift law (conditioning effect, finding F1).

admitted_families.name: abstention gaps (not counterexamples: reference arm abstains too)
admitted_families.description: int64 one-hot, empty output, raising kernel: every tolerance-bearing law and the reference arm answer INCONCLUSIVE, which gate.py prints as PASS 0/9. The first two are FAILed by output_type_matches_input; the third cannot be closed by any law.

added_laws.name: output_type_matches_input (active, tolerance-free)
added_laws.statement: y.shape == x.shape and y.dtype is a floating dtype. Structural guard for the kernel's type, which the harness does not enforce; the value law defers to it. For softmax a non-floating output is provably wrong on every row of width >= 2 (exact values lie strictly inside (0,1)).

added_laws.name: log_ratio_to_input (active; the completion)
added_laws.statement: Within every row, every judgeable entry y_j > 0 and x_j - log y_j is constant across j (y proportional to exp(x)). With rows_sum_to_one this is the graph of softmax (Theorem 2). Judgeable = entries whose exact value exp(x_j - max) is a normal number of y's dtype (all, on the gate's domain).
added_laws.tolerance: residual r = centred ((x - max) - log y) per row; residual_ratio(r, 0, dtype=y.dtype, n=row width) = ||r||_inf / (eps * max(log2 n, 1)) < 30 (DEFAULT_THRESH). A residual in log y is a relative error in y, so the harness's unit-scale fallback applies. Bound for a correct float32 kernel: per-entry relative error <= (D/2 + 2.5) eps (D = row logit range; exponent formation D*eps/2, exp 1 ulp, divide 0.5 ulp, cast 0.5 ulp); normalizer cancels in centring; centring at most doubles: ratio <= (D+5)/log2 n ~ 4 at n=8. Measured max 1.24 (seed 42), 1.2 over 20 further seeds, 0 false alarms.

added_laws.name: gibbs_log_linear (inactive factoring half, scale-free)
added_laws.statement: (x_j, log y_j) collinear within each row: y is a Gibbs distribution of x at some per-row temperature (beta = 0 included). Least-squares line in centred coordinates, sup-norm residual.
added_laws.tolerance: same residual_ratio convention, threshold 30; measured max 1.12

added_laws.name: unit_temperature (inactive factoring half, scale-fixing)
added_laws.statement: For rows with distinct judgeable logits: log y[argmax x] - log y[argmin x] = max x - min x. log_ratio_to_input <=> gibbs_log_linear and unit_temperature (SoftmaxBundle.factoring); the halves are independent (temperature_half vs curved_gibbs).
added_laws.tolerance: same residual_ratio convention, threshold 30; measured max 1.37

correct_variants_checked: correct_variants/base2_with_log2e_f32.py (exp2 with log2(e) factor, float32 throughout)
correct_variants/reciprocal_multiply_f32.py (multiply by float32 reciprocal of the row sum)

report.remarks_on_formal_ambiguity: (1) The completeness theorem is relative to the primitive: exp_pos/exp_add are satisfied by 2^x and by the constant 1, so Lean pins K to 'softmax w.r.t. whatever exp the law computes with'. primitive_mismatch.py makes this concrete: swapping np.exp for np.exp2 inside laws.py leaves the Lean proof compiling verbatim while the law accepts admitted/temperature_base2.py (0/18 cases failed) and rejects reference.py (14/18). Binding the primitive to e^x rests on np.exp (float64, ≤1 ulp), outside the proof. (2) 'Over the reals' is an idealization: floats are not a field; the Lean predicates are exact equalities and the gate's laws are tolerance tests (except shape and unit interval), so float-level completeness is empirical, and in the noise band η ∈ [1e-5, 3.2e-5] the completed declarative arm is strictly stricter than the reference arm (259 declarative-only rejections, 0 reference-only, out of 5940 cases). (3) The Lean reference row is the unshifted exp x_i / Σ exp x_j; reference.py subtracts the row max; softmax_sub proves they coincide, but this uses exp_add, so the max-subtracted and unshifted forms are only provably equal under that assumption. (4) The bundle has no dtype law: a float16 output passes both arms (probes/float16_output.py); an uncast float64 output is rejected by SHIFT_INVARIANCE only via eps accounting (probes/float64_output.py). Dtype is outside 'over the reals' and was deliberately not added. (5) n = 1 rows are unobservable by any arm on this domain (2 of 9 rungs), so 7/9 is the ceiling for a kernel wrong on every n > 1 row. (6) INCONCLUSIVE/abstention, non-finite values, and the gate's one sampled shift per row (scale 44.4) are not modelled in Lean; Lean's ShiftInvariant quantifies over every per-row constant.
report.statement_vs_laws: Lean states exact equalities over an ordered field; laws.py checks floating-point forms with the harness's normalized test ratio. Companion theorems in the same file: row_unique, row_zero_of_const, standardize_satisfies (existence: r > 0, r²·Σ(x−mean x)² = n ⇒ r·(x − mean x) satisfies the bundle), zero_row_satisfies_on_const, bundle_implies_shift_invariance, eps_breaks_exact_unit_variance. primitive_assumptions: Lean: no square root is assumed to exist in the field; the reciprocal standard deviation enters standardize_satisfies as a hypothesis r > 0 with r * r * Σ(x i − mean x)² = n, and eps_breaks_exact_unit_variance as r * r * (Σ centered² + eps * n) = n.
Lean: division is the field's a / b = a * b⁻¹ (Lean.Grind.Field); it is used only with the denominator ones (n+1) = Σ 1, proved non-zero (0 < ones (n+1)).

Lean: the order is only a preorder compatible with + and * (Lean.Grind.OrderedRing: 0 < 1, multiplication by a positive element preserves <) with < related to ≤ by Std.LawfulOrderLT; no totality, no Archimedean property, no completeness.

report.remarks_on_formal_ambiguity: (1) 'Characterizes the reference' is only meaningful up to tolerance: reference.py has eps = 1e-5 inside the root, so in exact arithmetic it does NOT satisfy UNIT_VARIANCE (Σy² = n·var/(var+eps) < n; Lean: eps_breaks_exact_unit_variance) and is admitted by the old and the completed bundle only through rows_have_unit_variance's budget 30·eps32·n; the exact completed bundle characterizes layernorm at eps = 0. Neither arm can pin eps on this domain (results/eps_sweep.txt). (2) UNIT_VARIANCE's wording 'except rows a constant input zeroed' is implemented as an abstention, not as an assertion that such rows are zero; that abstention is precisely what leaves the constant-row value free in the old bundle, and the completing law is what forces it to zero (Lean: row_zero_of_const). In floating point eps > 0 is forced not by any statistical law but by FINITE_OUTPUT at the n = 1 rungs (eps = 0 gives 0/0). (3) 'K : R^{m×n} → R^{m×n}' in the question makes the shape law a typing fact, but the harness's bundle has no shape law and admits a constant 1×2 output, so a structural law is needed at the gate even though it is not mathematics. (4) The README's criterion for a wrong kernel is 'the reference arm rejects', and the reference arm measures in the kernel's output dtype: a float16-returning kernel is accepted by both arms, a float64-returning one rejected by both (the old bundle rejects it incidentally via shift_invariance on the float32-quantized partner); no dtype law was added, and this is noted as a reference-arm blind spot (results/dtype_probe.txt). (5) Theorem A (K_rank indistinguishable from layernorm by any unary/equivariance/idempotence/order law) holds for n ≥ 3 on rows with distinct entries; for n = 2 the sphere in H is two points, and with ties the stable-argsort K_rank is not permutation-equivariant (probability 0 under the gate's draws). (6) The Lean UnitVariance is Σy² = n, which is population variance 1 given zero mean; the two hypotheses always appear together.
report.statement_vs_laws: The Lean statement uses exact equalities where laws.py uses tolerances: PosAffine is an existential ∃ a > 0, b, y i = a * x i + b, whereas the law computes the least-squares slope lambda = <c,d>/<c,c> on centered rows, FAILs on lambda <= 0 (exact sign test) and otherwise requires residual_ratio(d, lambda*c) < 30 (equivalent in exact arithmetic: the residual is zero iff the law holds and then lambda = a); ZeroMean is vsum y = 0 vs |mean| <= 30·eps·n·max(|y|,1); UnitVariance is Σy² = n vs |var(y) − 1| <= 30·eps·n. The Lean world is an abstract field with a compatible preorder, with no rounding model, no float32/float64 distinction and no dtype; laws.py judges float32 outputs with float64 accumulation. Lean has no shape law (the matrix type Fin m → Fin n → F is the shape) and no finiteness law (vacuous over a field), while laws.py adds output_shape_matches_input and the bundle keeps outputs_are_finite. Lean proves shift_invariance as a consequence (bundle_implies_shift_invariance); the gate still evaluates it as a law since bundle.yaml is fixed. The Lean hypotheses quantify over all inputs x; the gate evaluates 18 fixed cases (seed 42), so Lean says nothing about kernels correct on those 18 and wrong elsewhere.
report.notes: Negative findings and dead ends recorded in RESULT.md §3: (a) eps blindness of both arms on this domain (eps' in [1e-6, 1e-4] inside, [1e-6, 1e-5] outside indistinguishable from the reference); (b) the invariance/equivariance/idempotence/monotonicity vocabulary cannot complete the bundle (Theorem A, K_rank; cubed is the continuous counterpart), which is why a relational law was necessary; (c) the gate's case set has no constant row with n >= 2, so the constant-row freedom of the old bundle is unreachable by either arm on the gate (beyond_gate/, results/constant_rows.txt); (d) the OLD bundle's rows_have_unit_variance and shift_invariance give false alarms on the reference itself when var(x) <~ 300·eps (block B of results/law_robustness.txt), while the new law has no false alarm in any regime tried; (e) correct_variants/rsqrt_reciprocal.py (one-pass float32 variance) is rejected by the reference arm on 8 of 900 domain groups and sits at ratio 25.3 on the gate's seed — it is correct only at the gate's resolution; (f) output dtype: float64 output rejected by both arms (incidentally), float16 output accepted by both; no dtype law added by the README's criterion.
